newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end lower in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end lower in choppy trade.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Friday's Tokyo session lower in choppy trade, after a stab at the upside faltered and dealers were forced to liquidate long positions, traders said.
June closed down 0.38 at 126.71, after rising as high as 127.04 in the afternoon.
Turnover on the contract was 50,863 lots.

"The market was quite volatile in the latter half of the afternoon. Some dealers were forced to cover long positions after failing in an attempt to push the market through buy-stops on the upside," said a brokerage house trader.
Afternoon trade was driven mainly by dealer plays rather than fundamentals, traders said.
They added that comments by key government officials after the end of the morning session had only limited impact on JGBs.
Kabun Muto, the head of Japan's Management and Coordination Agency, said Japan should raise its official discount rate by the end of this year to discourage capital outflows.
Construction Minister Shizuka Kamei said the steep fall in the yen was pushing up import prices of construction materials and undermining the government's efforts to reduce costs at public works.
"Muto had made similar remarks earlier this week, so the impact was limited. Kamei's comments were also ignored," said a trader at another brokerage house.
Muto urged the Bank of Japan (BOJ) on Tuesday to consider the possibility of raising the official discount rate.

JGB futures started out the day lower on comments made on Thursday by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, that market players had become overly pessimistic about Japan's economic outlook.
Sakakibara also said he believed this pessimism was reflected in a recent fall in long-term interest rates.
Traders said an overnight rumour in the euroyen futures market that the BOJ may raise short-term rates to prevent a further fall in the yen also had a negative impact on JGBs.
Buying briefly emerged after the BOJ's outright bond buying operation at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT), but was short-lived.
There had been speculation that the BOJ might be considering cutting back the amount of its monthly outright bond purchases.
This speculation emerged when the BOJ, contrary to market expectations, failed to conduct bond purchases on Wednesday and Thursday, traders said.
Cash JGBs were also weaker, but some public fund bodies were detected buying the benchmark 182nd JGBs, traders said.
The yield of the 182nd JGBs stood at 2.160 percent as of 5.15 p.m. (0815 GMT), up from 2.145 percent on Thursday.
"Investors were reluctant to buy cash JGBs as the bond market is awash with new corporate bonds. More companies may tap the primary market next week, so people were cautious," said the first trader.
Over 300 billion yen worth of new corporate bonds have been launched this week.
-- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
